structure: Part 5, Address book (repos/trade-imports-ins-tests at 3c7ea8a). Read in full: the 7 animals address-book specs under tests/animals/e2e/features/address-book (address-book-navigation 1 test, addresses-add-handshake 2, addresses-copied 4, addresses-edit 6, addresses-picker 1, addresses-read-only 3 test bodies, one of them parameterised over the 5 party roles so 11 cases, addresses-submit-freeze 2); the 7 INS address-book specs under tests/ins/e2e/features/address-book (address-book 1, address-book-add-handshake-guard 1, address-book-auth 2, address-book-cross-user-visibility 1, address-book-delete 2, address-book-edit 2, address-book-persistence 1); the animals page objects addresses-page, party-picker-page, party-edit-page and contact-address-page (plus the role/slug/heading wiring in page-objects/animals/index.ts and the Address book and Dashboard link locators in page-objects/shared/base-page.ts, looked up to name what the specs click); the INS address-book page objects list, view, add, edit, delete and the shared form page; the shared E2E address-book fixtures (domain/shared/fixtures/e2e-address-book.ts); the Mongo address document model; and the address-book HTTP API client. Covered: the Consignment addresses hub and its per-role Add / Change / Edit details links; the five party pickers (page size, view details, search, newest-first pagination, no-JS selection carried across pages, Add a new address link and its stub-mode absence); the copy-not-link rule for picked addresses (book edits and soft deletes never reach a draft, a submitted notification or an amendment); the per-notification Edit address details form (labels, hint, prefill, validation messages, cancel return, isolation from the book and other notifications) for party roles and the contact address; the review-page error for a copied address that breaks the notification's rules and how it blocks continue and submit; the add handshake from the journey to the INS add page and back, its cancel path and its journey-type guard; navigation between the animals dashboard and the INS address book; and the INS address book's list, add, edit (full replace), delete (soft, confirmed), sign-in redirect, organisation-wide visibility, persistence and stored fields. Page-object-only surfaces no spec exercises (the INS view page, the list empty state, the standalone add cancel, INS form validation) are recorded as inferred or gap.

claims.statement: The address book API keeps each organisation's addresses under /organisation/{organisationId}/addresses, and requires a Trade-Imports-Organisation-Id header matching the organisation in the path.
The address book service relies on its callers for authentication and organisation scoping rather than authenticating requests itself.
claims.quote: The address book runs no authentication of its own
claims.note: Security-relevant: stated in general terms only.

claims.statement: The address book API lists an organisation's live addresses newest first, as a page of items with a total count, searchable with a q query; soft-deleted records are omitted.
The address book API creates an address with a POST of the record and replaces one with a PUT of the whole record.
claims.quote:
Replaces an address. The API takes the whole record, so the caller passes
   * the current one with the fields it wants changed already applied.

claims.statement: The address book API returns one address by id, including a soft-deleted one with deleted: true; this is the only way to detect a deletion.
claims.quote:
One address by id, including soft-deleted tombstones (`deleted: true`).
   * List endpoints omit tombstones; this is the only way to detect a deletion.

claims.statement: The address book API's delete is a soft delete that answers 204 and is idempotent.
claims.quote:
Soft-deletes an address (204, idempotent). The tombstone stays readable via
   * {@link getAddress}; list/search no longer return it.

claims.statement: An address book record as the API returns it has id, name, address line 1, optional address line 2, town or city, optional county, postcode, country code, phone, email and a deleted flag.
